title: Ἱστορίαι / Chiliades (Book of Histories); «Хилиады» («Книга историй»)
author: John Tzetzes
genre: Antiquarian-didactic poem in political verse; self-commentary on his letters
edition: Kiessling 1826, public domain (https://books.google.com/books?id=dG0GAAAAQAAJ); Leone 1968, 2nd ed. 2007. The volunteer English translation is based on Kiessling.
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Иоанн Цец': only excerpts, in Памятники византийской литературы IX–XIV вв. (1969), pp. 252–259. No fuller Russian translation found.
en_evidence: Volunteer translation (Untila, Berkowitz, Ramiotis, Dogani et al.; mitologia.pt), made from Kiessling 1826. It calls itself a 'tentative first edition' with minimal notes; last edit 2024. https://archive.org/details/TzetzesCHILIADES; also on theoi.com.
other_translations: No complete French, German, Italian or Spanish translation found (search not exhaustive).
value: Preserves fragments and testimonia of over 200 ancient authors. A key text for source criticism and for Byzantine teaching of the classics, and it contains Alexander anecdotes. No annotated scholarly translation exists in any language. A source-tracing commentary is exactly the apparatus Neoscholia offers.
ai_feasibility: High. Political verse reads almost like prose. The main work is identifying sources, which AI does well but every case needs checking against TLG and the fragment editions.
pilot_unit: Chiliad I (about 1,000 verses, opening with Croesus), or a thematic dossier of the Alexander histories
